athletes.name: Abdulla Al Tamimi
athletes.standfirst: Abdulla Al-Tamimi is a Qatari squash player who's storming his way up the international rankings with impressive performances.
bio: Abdulla Al-Tamimi's career has been on an upward trajectory ever since turning pro in 2011. The Qatari number one broke into the world top 70 in 2014 and reached the final of three PSA World Tour events, although fell just short of taking top honours in each of them.

However, the wait for a first PSA World Tour win ended in March 2016, when Al-Tamimi triumphed at the Atlanta Open. More success followed swiftly, with the Qatar Circuit No. 3 title sealed the same month and the Australian Open in August.
Fast forward to 2022 and Al-Tamimi sits in the top 30 of the Men's PSA World Squash Rankings thanks to wins everywhere from Tauranga in New Zealand to Gorgan in Iran.

athletes.name: Adel 'Big Bird' Anouche
athletes.standfirst: Born in Algeria but representing the UAE, Adel 'Big Bird' Anouche is a star on the Street Fighter scene, known for his Ken and Rashid play.
bio: Though born in Algeria, Adel 'Big Bird' Anouche has lived most of his life in the United Arab Emirates. The Middle Eastern nation has gradually become recognised as a hotbed of dedicated Street Fighter play thanks to a group of highly skilled locals and a tendency to fly in big names like Daigo 'The Beast' Umehara.

Big Bird grew up around fighting games. "I've always loved playing Street Fighter," he says. "I've most likely played every Street Fighter there is. I started playing competitively in 2012 with SFIV. At first, I was just playing with my friend Angrybird for fun. We went to our local arcade and got mopped by the local players there even though I thought I was 'good.' I learned that the game's much deeper than just learning how to do fireballs, shoryukens, supers and ultras – even though I was losing, I still enjoyed playing, and it only made me want to play more and more."

It wasn't long before he began making a name for himself on the competitive circuit: "One day, there was a local tournament organised by my friend, and he invited us over. I entered and got third place. From there on out, I've entered almost every local tournament in the country up until today."

He was soon claiming big-name international scalps alongside his local success – Poongko and Xian, to name a couple – but it was his head-turning performance at Red Bull Kumite in 2016 that brought him to the attention of many fans.

Big Bird not only won the qualification tournament overall, but did so while only dropping a single game to fellow qualifier Valentin 'Valmaster' Petit in the last game of the day. In the tournament proper, he accounted for local favourite Alioune Camara in the opening game, going on to knock out Xian and Gamerbee before running out of momentum against Kazunoko to take fifth place overall.

Now regularly challenging for honours, Big Bird is consistently near the top of the global Capcom Pro Tour ranking and has two victories at the all-star Red Bull Kumite tournament to his name. He claimed his first crown in South Africa in 2023 before rising to the top once again in Paris in 2025.

athletes.name: Ahmed 'AAMEGHESSIB' Al Meghessib
athletes.standfirst: Qatari Ahmed 'AAMEGHESSIB' Al Meghessib has earned his bragging rights as one of the top FIFA players in the Middle East.
bio: A graduate of the Aspire Academy, Ahmed 'AAMEGHESSIB' Al Meghessib has developed into a talented midfielder and is also one of the top FIFA players in the whole of the Middle East.

As well as playing professionally for a number of Qatari clubs, Ahmed has carved out a hugely successful esports career, first making waves on the world stage in 2017 when he stormed through the regional finals to represent the Rest of the World at the FIFA Interactive World Cup.
Now the face of Red Bull Back-2-Back, a unique esport platform for FIFA 21 on PlayStation 5, Ahmed represents Ooredoo Thunders and the Qatar National esports team.

athletes.name: Albert Arenas
athletes.standfirst: Crowned the Moto3™ World Champion in 2020, Spanish rider Albert Arenas is now chasing glory in Moto2™ with Red Bull KTM Ajo.
bio: Albert Arenas was just four years old when he first started riding mini motorcycles and was immediately hooked. He soon began competing in junior championships and showed plenty of promise during his four-year spell in the FIM CEV Repsol series (now known as the Junior World Championship).

In his final season at junior level in 2015, Albert claimed second place in the championship after securing three wins. This earned the Spanish rider a place with the Aspar Team and then the Peugeot MC Saxoprint team, making several appearances for both during the 2016 Moto3™ World Championship.

Albert rejoined the Aspar Team in 2017 and earned a full-time place in Moto3™. After a season of adapting, he was able to secure his first victory at the French Grand Prix in 2018. Two podiums and another win came in 2019 as he finished 11th in the overall standings, but it was 2020 that was a year to remember for the Spaniard.

Having come back from injury late in 2019, Albert started the new season with consecutive victories in Qatar and Jerez. He would then win again in Austria and secure two more podium finishes on the way to being crowned Moto3™ world champion at the age of 24.

Albert moved up to the Moto2™ World Championship in 2021 and steadily adapted to the new challenge. He continued to make progress in 2022 as he finished 10th or better in eight races and ended the campaign in 12th place overall.

He then joined Red Bull KTM Ajo for his third season in the intermediate class and secured his first podium finish in Moto2™ in Spain. In 2024, he consistently battled inside the top 10 and ended the year in 14th overall.

2025 proved to be Albert's most successful year in Moto2™ to date as he recorded his best finish in Italy (second) on the way to finishing the season in eighth place overall. He'll hope to challenge more regularly for podium places in 2026.

athletes.name: Almoez Ali
athletes.standfirst: Almoez Ali is Qatar's all-time top scorer at international level and helped shoot his country to their first-ever AFC Asian Cup win.
bio: Born in Sudan, Almoez Ali moved to Qatar as a young child and quickly developed a love for football. Inspired by Qatari legends such as Khalfan Ibrahim Khalfan and Hassan Al-Haydos, he was on the path to stardom from a very young age.

As an Aspire Academy graduate, Almoez first tasted international success with the Qatari U19 squad: helping them to win the U19 AFC Championship and booking Qatar's place at the U19 World Cup in 2014.

From there on, Almoez toured Europe to kick off his professional career with LASK Linz of Austria before making his mark with Cultural Leonesa in Spain's Segunda División B and becoming the first Qatari to score in the Spanish League.
Almoez returned to Qatar in 2016 to join Al-Duhail and became a key member of the team that won back-to-back league titles in 2016-17 and 2017-18.

In 2020, he captained the team to another league title before claiming a fourth title in 2023. His goals have also helped the team win numerous other trophies, including the Emir of Qatar Cup on four occasions and the Qatar Cup twice.

In 2016, Almoez made his official senior debut for the Qatari national team and soon became an integral member of the squad. However, it was in 2019 that he came to the fore for his country, helping them claim the AFC Asian Cup for the very first time. He was also recognised as the tournament's best player, as well as finishing as the top scorer.
Almoez made history again when he became the top scorer of the 2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup, scoring four goals across the tournament.

The following year, he started all three group matches during their first-ever appearance at the World Cup and in 2023, helped Qatar successfully defend their AFC Asian Cup title, scoring in the opening match and grabbing the winning goal in the semi-final against Iran.

Almoez enjoyed a fruitful 2023 as he scored eight goals for his country, the most important of which came in a World Cup qualifying game against Afghanistan. That goal saw Almoez surpass Mansour Muftah and become Qatar's all-time leading goalscorer.
Almoez continues to be a prolific scorer for his country and in 2026 once again played on the world's biggest stage as he made a single appearance for Qatar at the World Cup in North America.

athletes.name: Amar 'Amar' Al Naimi
athletes.standfirst: A hugely popular streamer, YouTuber and esports athlete, Germany's Amar Al-Naimi has played his way through the gaming world at top speed.
bio: Amar 'Amar' Al-Naimi found a way to turn his passion into his job and has never looked back. Despite being discouraged by some from pursuing a career in esports, the German made the decisive step in 2016 and has gone on to enjoy a wealth of success.

Initially excelling in the competitive Call of Duty world, Amar jumped to Fortnite and was crowned European Champion in 2019. This victory helped catapult him to the top of the Twitch charts – breaking the one million subscriber mark and becoming one of the most popular creators in Germany.
Still competing in titles such as VALORANT and Call of Duty, Amar now organises his own events and runs his own fashion label.

athletes.name: Andrea Adamo
athletes.standfirst: The 2023 FIM MX2 World Championship winner, Andrea Adamo is the latest world champion for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing and Italy's rising motocross star.
bio: Andrea Adamo is a rising star of motocross from Erice in Italy who's currently competing in the MX2 class of the FIM World Motocross Championship.
Andrea shot to fame in 2017 when he won the Honda EMX150 title. He spent the following four years making a name for himself by scoring some steadily improving results for Yamaha and then GASGAS.

The Sicilian rider ended his 2021 season by securing 14th-place overall and he accelerated his development the following term by achieving his first podium result with second at the Grand Prix of Lombardia in Italy.
The 2022 season saw Andrea take his form to new heights with numerous podiums and eighth-place overall, which culminated in him signing with Red Bull KTM Factory Racing for the 2023 season.

The move paid off for both Adamo and KTM in a big way, as he scored 11 podium finishes across the FIM MX2 World Championship season - including two Grands Prix victories – to hand the Italian his first world title on home soil at the penultimate GP and the powerhouse KTM squad another MX2 title to add to its huge collection.
The heir to the great Antonio Cairoli's crown as the next Italian motocross legend, watch for Adamo to go on from here to collect more world titles in the year's to come.

athletes.name: Antonia Abraham
athletes.standfirst: Part of a family dynasty of rowing in her native Chile, picking up medals and growing her reputation one competition at a time.
athletes.discipline: Rowing Quadruple Sculls / Rowing Light Weight / Rowing Pairs
bio: Antonia Abraham and her siblings are putting Chilean rowing on the map with impressive performances at international competitions. Antonia is one of four quadruplets and competes alongside her sister Melita, while her brothers Ignacio and Alfredo also represent their country on the world stage.

Antonia and her siblings started rowing thanks to a chance invitation from a friend of their brother Ignacio. While still in primary school, Antonia first went along to the lakes of the Regatta Club in Concepción, near her family home in San Pedro de la Paz. It was the first step on a path that's taking her around the world with her oars in hand.

Outstanding performances at the 2018 South American Games saw Antonia take W1x gold on her own plus further golds in the W4x, W2x and the W2- competitions with Melita. There have also been encouraging results in Europe, including silver at the Rowing World Cup, plus a slew of Pan-American Games medals of every colour.

athletes.name: Bjorn Riley
athletes.standfirst: An XCC World Cup winner, Bjorn Riley has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting talents in cross-country mountain biking.
bio: Growing up in Boulder, Colorado, it was Bjorn Riley's outdoor adventures with his family as a child that sparked his passion for mountain biking, and he began racing competitively at just 11 in 2013. Fast-forward to 2021, and the American decided to make the move to Europe to focus fully on his development with Trek Vaude – and it was a move which eventually paid off.

Riley began to make a name for himself during the 2024 season, winning both the U23 XCC and XCO World Cup races at Les Gets, along with securing multiple podium finishes throughout the season. He also produced a double victory on home soil, capturing the US National titles in Elite XCO and XCC in Macungie.

Following that stellar season, Riley made the leap up to the elite ranks as he signed with one of the world's top mountain bike teams, Scott-SRAM Factory Racing – and he didn't take long to prove himself on the big stages. In 2026, he secured his first Elite World Cup victory in the XCC at Pal Arinsal, Andorra, making a late pass on in-form French rider Adrien Boichis and holding him off in a thrilling sprint to the finish.
"Every race feels like the fulfilment of a dream. Winning is something you dream about your whole life, so actually doing it feels surreal," Riley said following the biggest win of his career.
He also claimed his third consecutive US Elite XCC national title before finishing fourth in the Elite XCC race at the 2026 UCI Mountain Bike World Championships in Val di Sole.

Known for his style and artistry on the track, Riley is also quite the creative mind away from it. He's a passionate artist who enjoys experimenting with different mediums – he even designed the artwork for his own US Champion Edition race bike.

athletes.name: Bora Altıntaş
athletes.standfirst: The rising BMX street rider who learned his skills on a home-made ramp setup and is putting the sport on the map in Turkey.
bio: Interested in basketball and athletics as a child, Bora Altıntaş first encountered BMX at the age of 13 through friends. Since then, BMX has never left the Turkish rider's life.

Working endlessly on his skills on the ramp he built using the door his father took from their own house, Bora continued to improve himself day by day. In 2014, the small skatepark that his father hand built in the park next to their house allowed Bora to go one step further.
His hard work was rewarded by winning the BMX Street Festival in Limassol, Cyprus three times between 2015 and 2016.
In 2017, he achieved his first success outside of Cyprus after claiming second place in the Turkey BMX Day and fourth place in the RideOnBmx competition held in Greece.

Having completed construction of the Fibera BMX Skatepark project in 2018, which he'd been planning for a while with the support of their parents, Bora also gained a top class skatepark to train on, paving the way for other successes in 2019.

Most notable was the renowned Nass Festival in England, which is one of the most important professional competitions in the world, where athletes can only participate by invitation. Bora achieved an important result there by taking the sixth place among 30 of the world's best athletes.
Bora then participated in the RideonBmx Battle in Thessaloniki, Greece the same year and managed to win with the team he led.

athletes.name: CapJay
athletes.standfirst: Capjay is the American street dancer wowing audiences with his musicality and technical excellence, moving between styles with the instinct of someone who refuses to be defined by just one.
bio: At three years old, he made his dance debut on the kids' TV show Hip Hop Harry, while honing his moves in his living room to a constant stream of Michael Jackson records his mum had on rotation.

In his teens, the self-taught hip-hop freestyler branched out from breaking into other street styles. Capjay's first love was basketball, but after entering a dance battle in Las Vegas, he was instantly hooked by the adrenaline of competition, the freedom of expression and the energy of the crowd. His dreams of becoming a basketball player were history.
A self-professed “dance addict,” Capjay moved to LA, determined to take his art and career to new heights.
As a beat maker, he brings a musical instinct to his dancing, fusing a plethora of hip-hop styles with clever wordplay, popping, intricate footwork and limit-defying power moves.

When he's not competing, he's thinking about dance: watching battles, choreographing, producing music for dancers on SoundCloud under the moniker Capbeats and plotting his next move. He's already looking beyond dance, too, with ambitions to expand his world into fashion - a natural progression for someone known for his collection of fly hats.

“My dream is for hip-hop dancers to reach the same level as rappers and artists when it comes to fame and love. I want to be one of the best hip-hop dancers to ever exist, one of those pillars that grows our culture and brings a whole bunch of attention to what we're doing over here in the US. I want to touch the choreography world and spill my experience as a mentor, inspiring younger peeps to go crazy in battles.”

In 2025, he claimed double gold at the World DanceSport Federation World Championship in Bucharest, Romania, winning both the Youth Hip-Hop Freestyle 1 vs 1 and Adult Freestyle 2 vs 2 (alongside his partner Taktic). He consolidated this momentum by capturing the Red Bull Dance Your Style South USA title in Tampa, before advancing to the Red Bull Dance Your Style National Final USA, where he built a rapidly growing global fanbase.

The victories continued into 2026. In July, he won the 2 vs 2 hip-hop battle at Italy’s prestigious Give It Up, partnering with Red Bull All Star The D Soraki - a collaboration that confirmed his standing among the street dance elite.

He is the founder of three battle platforms: The Deepend Sesh, District 12X and Shadow Park. With these he is enabling dancers to test and grow their skills, while being a globally sought-after workshop teacher and judge.

athletes.name: César Arévalo
athletes.standfirst: An acrobatic paraglider specialising in gravity-defying manoeuvres, pushing the capabilities of the pilot and his team to the limit. Driven to overcome fear and explore new boundaries.
bio: César is ranked number one on the American continent and has achieved international results that cement his status as one of the best acrobatic paragliders in the world. Among his triumphs are the first place in the 2022 Synchronization World Cup in Albania and fourth place in the World Acro Cup 2025. Since beginning his sports career in acrobatics at age 19, he has maintained a consistent position in the top 10 worldwide.

Recognised for his discipline, precision, and methodical approach, César not only dominates aerial acrobatics but has also expanded his skills into cross-country and hike & fly, facing the challenges of exploration, endurance, and decision-making in extreme environments. His passion for overcoming fear and pushing new limits has led him to evolve as a driver without compromising safety, making him a benchmark of high performance.

His story began at the age of four, when he made his first tandem flight with his father. At 13, he took his first solo flight; at 17, he travelled abroad for the first time to train in Nepal, laying the foundations of his paragliding career.

Trained in an era of limited access to information, Caesar developed a distinctive style grounded in direct experience and in-depth analysis. Today, his mindset motivates him to share his knowledge with the community, helping new generations of pilots develop safer, more efficient processes.
In addition to competing, he is a flight safety instructor and creator of educational content in English and Spanish, inspiring pilots and adventurers worldwide to experience the magic of flying.

athletes.name: Cooper DeJean
athletes.standfirst: From small-town Iowa to football’s biggest stage, Cooper DeJean has built his game on versatility, instinct and a knack for making big plays when it matters most.
bio: Cooper DeJean has never fit neatly into one position. Growing up in Odebolt, Iowa, a small town with no stoplights, just stop signs and yield signs, he was the kind of athlete who could seemingly do it all. DeJean competed in football, basketball, baseball and track at OABCIG High School, starring on both sides of the football field as a quarterback and defensive back while helping lead his team to back-to-back state championships.

DeJean stayed close to home at the University of Iowa, where that versatility became his calling card. Whether shutting down receivers, creating turnovers or changing a game as a punt returner, he developed into one of college football’s most exciting defensive players, earning unanimous All-American honors and Big Ten Defensive Back of the Year.
That same ability to impact a game followed him to Philadelphia after being selected No. 40 overall pick in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft.
DeJean quickly became an important piece of Philadelphia’s defense, but his career-defining moment came on the biggest stage.

Playing in Super Bowl LIX on his 22nd birthday, DeJean stepped in front of a Patrick Mahomes pass and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown, helping the Eagles capture their second Super Bowl championship and delivering one of the game’s defining plays.
He has continued to build from there, earning First-Team All-Pro honors and a Pro Bowl selection while establishing himself among the NFL’s top young defensive players.

From a town without a single stoplight to football’s biggest stage, DeJean has built his career on versatility, confidence and showing up when the moment calls for it. And if his start is any indication, there are plenty more big moments ahead.

athletes.name: Courage Adams
athletes.standfirst: From world-record manuals to X Games gold, Courage Adams has established himself as one of the defining BMX Street riders of his generation.
bio: Born in Benin City, Nigeria, Courage Adams moved to northern Spain with his family at the age of five. It wasn't until he was 12 that he discovered BMX, but from the moment he first rode a bike, he knew he had found his passion. Hours spent at his local skatepark quickly turned into an obsession, and before long he was dedicating himself to mastering the technical side of BMX Street.

Adams announced himself to the professional scene at just 16 years old when he finished second at the 2012 O Marisquiño contest in Vigo – an achievement which proved to be the beginning of a remarkable rise as he developed into one of the most exciting and complete riders in BMX. Combining his power and creativity with extraordinary bike control, he has earned a reputation for pushing the boundaries of what's possible on the front and back wheel.

Equally at home competing on the biggest stages or filming progressive street edits, Adams has become synonymous with technical riding. His signature manual and nose manual combinations have redefined modern BMX Street, blending precision, balance and flow in a way few riders can match. Whether competing at FISE Montpellier, X Games or O Marisquiño, his unique style has made him one of the sport's standout performers.

His success has been matched by an impressive list of achievements. Adams has claimed multiple victories at FISE Montpellier, won O Marisquiño on numerous occasions and, in 2023, set a world record by riding a remarkable 400m nose manual. That same year he earned his first X Games medal with silver in BMX Street before adding bronze in 2024 and, after overcoming a shoulder injury, capturing his maiden X Games gold in Osaka in 2025.

Away from competition, Adams has never forgotten his roots. Returning regularly to Nigeria, he has worked to help grow BMX in the country, supporting the creation of its first dedicated BMX park and inspiring a new generation of riders to discover the sport that transformed his own life. His commitment to giving back has made him as respected off the bike as he is on it.

athletes.name: Courtney Atkinson
athletes.standfirst: A multiple Australian Triathlete of the Year and national team hero, Courtney Atkinson is a frequent podium finisher on the World Cup circuit.
bio: Courtney Atkinson is one of Australia’s top athletes, with an impressive medal haul to boot thanks to a multitude of triathlon titles. As a teenager growing up around Mackay, Australia, Courtney had a passion for the outdoors.

“I grew up on the Gold Coast dreaming of becoming a Surf Life Saving Ironman racing in big waves, before I got into triathlon,” he says. It was around the age of 16 and 17 that Courtney decided to focus exclusively on triathlon, and the Queensland native won four consecutive Australian Junior Triathlon Championships from 1996 to 1999.
Between 2002 and 2004, Courtney’s achievement in his sport was recognised when he took the title of Australia’s Triathlete of the Year award for three consecutive years.

A national triathlon team member with a myriad of ITU World Cup wins and podium finishes under his belt, Courtney also earned himself a spot on the Australian team for Beijing in 2008, where he finished in a respectable 11th place.

As an Australian Elite national team member, he also competed at London in 2012, achieving yet another top 20 finish. In 2013, Courtney decided to turn his hand to longer distance racing, a change in tack which prompted a two-year sabbatical from International Triathlon Union (ITU) racing pursuits.

More success soon followed in his first event in Cairns and he put in a strong showing at the notoriously tough 226km Melbourne IRONMAN – with a time of just over eight hours – before switching back to longer distances in 2015.

Since then Courtney has continued to place highly in ITU events around the world, placing first at races everywhere from Singapore to New South Wales. But while he continues to dedicate himself to his punishing training regimen in the quest for more sporting accolades, his ultimate goal remains a humble one: “to simply be a great father and a happy man.”

athletes.name: Dania Akeel
athletes.standfirst: A former motorcycle racer, Saudi Arabia's Dania Akeel entered the world of rally-raid in 2021 and has won stages in both the Dakar and Abu Dhabi Rally.
bio: After achieving a degree in modern history and politics from Royal Holloway University in London, Dania moved to the UAE to complete a Master's degree in international business. While in Dubai, she got a motorcycle licence and began riding at the Dubai Autodrome racetrack.

It didn't take long before Dania sought out competition, and after receiving the first Saudi female license for motorcycle circuit racing, she contested the Ducati Cup in the UAE National Sportsbike Superseries 2019-20 season. Named the Rookie of the Year, she suffered a nasty injury in early 2020 after coming off her bike at a race meeting in Bahrain.

During her recovery, she decided to move back to Jeddah and soon discovered an interest in rally racing, largely because Saudi Arabia was home to the legendary Dakar Rally. She began competing in the FIA World Cup for Cross Country Bajas and dreamed of one day competing on home soil in the Dakar.

This dream became a reality in 2022, when Dania competed in the T3 category for South Racing Can-Am, finishing a credible eighth. “The Dakar was unbelievable. I really had a great time, and I saw how my driving developed over the course of the 12 stages, and I was very happy to see that progression,” Dania revealed to the official Dakar Rally website.

Dania returned to the Dakar in 2023 and once again completed all 12 stages. After success in the 2023 FIA World Cup for Cross-Country Bajas, Dania put in another good showing in the 2024 Dakar in the T3 category and went even better in the 2025 edition, where she scored an historic win on the punishing Stage 10 in Saudi Arabia's infamous Empty Quarter.

The following year saw her take third place overall in the 2025 FIA Rally-Raid World Championship Challenger Class in a campaign which included becoming the first woman to take the Challenger Class win at the Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge.
In 2026, she was back at the Dakar, where she finished eighth in the Challenger category and recorded seven stage podiums across the rally.

athletes.name: David Alonso
athletes.standfirst: The record-breaking 2024 Moto3™ champion, Colombian David Alonso is now chasing glory in the Moto2™ World Championship.
bio: From a young age, David Alonso loved watching motorbikes on TV with his parents, so when he made the leap into the world of racing, he had the full support of his family.

Excelling in various race series, the Colombian initially tasted success in CEV when riding an 85GP. Needing victory in the final race of the season to win the championship, he grabbed first place on the final lap to claim the title. "I realised that until you pass the flag, nothing is decided."
Always willing to put in plenty of hard work, David won the European Talent Cup in 2020 and the Red Bull MotoGP™ Rookies Cup in 2021.

These impressive results led to David being signed by the Gas Gas Aspar Team and in 2021 he made his Moto3™ World Championship debut, replacing the injured Sergio García at the Emilia Romagna GP. The following season he made his second start at the Portuguese GP as a wildcard rider.

In 2023, David made his full debut in the Moto3™ World Championship with the GAS GAS Aspar Team and made it clear very quickly that he's a champion in waiting. It took him just four Grands Prix to score his first podium, a second place at the Spanish GP, before going on to score four victories and another three second places to finish the season third overall in the Moto3™ World Championship to complete a remarkable debut season.

Staying with the newly-named CFMOTO Aspar Team for 2024, David put Colombia on top of the motorcycle racing world for the very first time with an incredible season that saw him ride to the Moto3™ world title with an incredible 14 wins from 20 starts – setting the record for the most wins in a season in the process.

On the back of his title win, David secured a place in Moto2™ for the 2025 season with his CFMOTO Aspar Team. It didn't take him long to make his mark as he scored his first podium in his seventh race. He then went on to claim a handful of podiums as well as a maiden victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix.
Entering the 2026 season with plenty of confidence, David will be seeking to add to his tally of victories as he looks to challenge for the title.

athletes.name: Ege 'Ar7' Arseven
athletes.standfirst: A member of FUT Esports and one of Türkiye's leading EA Sports FC content creators, Ege 'Ar7' Arseven is the go-to streamer for digital soccer fans.
bio: When it comes to EA Sports FC and the FIFA video game series, Ege 'Ar7' Arseven is the man keeping fans in Türkiye up to date and entertained via his beloved livestreams and video content.

A long time player of the series, Ar7 started live broadcasting his matches with the release of FIFA19 and joined the FUT Esports team in June of the same year. He's participated in tournaments including FutbolistAnbul, Blacki Cup, FIFAe Club Series, eSüperLig, FC Pro 24 Open, eTürkiye Cup and DreamHack Summer 2024 with the team since then, alongside developing a devoted audience for his content, which is renowned for his vibrant energy, lightheartedness and charisma.

athletes.name: Ehab Amin
athletes.standfirst: A defensive specialist who played college basketball in the United States, Egypt’s Ehab Amin is now the star point guard at Al Ahly.
bio: Born in Alexandria in Egypt, Ehab Amin was interested in sports from a young age and competed in swimming and football. However, it wasn’t long before he developed a love of basketball and joined the Alexandria Sporting Club. During his 11 years with the team he won the Egyptian Basketball Super League and the Egypt Basketball Cup.

In 2013, Ehab moved to the United States to attend St John's Northwestern Military Academy, where he suffered a serious back injury that prevented him from playing. Despite the setback, he was offered a scholarship to play college basketball for Texas A&M–Corpus Christi.

A regular starter in college, Ehab was named in the Southland All-Defensive Team during his junior season and led the NCAA Division I in steals. Following another injury, he made the move to the Oregon Ducks where he finished his college career.

In the summer of 2019, Ehab signed his first professional contract as he joined Al Ahly of the Egyptian Basketball Super League. In his time with the club, he has won the Egyptian Premier League on three occasions, as well as beind named MVP three times.
As well as starring for his club team, the point guard is also a regular starter for the Egyptian national team, having made his debut at senior level in 2015.

athletes.name: Eli Tomac
athletes.standfirst: One of the greatest riders in motocross and supercross history, Eli Tomac has 100+ victories and built a legacy through unmatched speed, relentless determination and championship-winning performances.
bio: Growing up in Cortez, Colorado, racing was part of Eli Tomac's DNA. His father, John Tomac, was one of America's greatest mountain bike racers, and competition was simply part of everyday life. While bicycles were always nearby, Eli quickly found his passion on two wheels powered by engines. By the time he reached the amateur ranks, he had become one of the country's most highly decorated young motocross riders, collecting national titles and establishing himself as one of the sport's brightest prospects.

Tomac turned professional in 2010 and immediately announced himself by winning his very first AMA Pro Motocross race—an achievement few riders have ever matched. That breakthrough launched one of the most successful careers of the modern era. After capturing both AMA 250 Supercross West and AMA 250 Motocross championships, he graduated to the premier 450 class, where his explosive riding style, remarkable fitness and ability to charge through the field quickly became legendary. By capturing six AMA 450-class championships, Eli Tomac earned his place among the greatest riders ever to line up behind the gate.

Eli Tomac is widely regarded as one of the greatest riders in American motocross history. Across more than a decade of elite competition, he has earned multiple AMA Supercross and Pro Motocross championships while becoming one of only a handful of riders to surpass 100 professional race victories. Tomac joined the Red Bull KTM Factory Racing team in 2026. His relentless work ethic, incredible late-race speed and longevity have made him a benchmark for generations of riders and a fan favorite wherever he competes.

athletes.name: Emma Aicher
athletes.standfirst: An Olympic and Junior World Championship medalist, German slalom and Super-G specialist Emma Aicher is one of alpine skiing's brightest young talents.
athletes.discipline: Alpine Skiing Giantslalom / Alpine Skiing Slalom
bio: Born and raised in the Swedish town of Sundsvall, where her Swedish and German parents were living, skiing runs through Emma Aicher's veins.
She strapped on skis almost as soon as she could walk and joined the local Slalomklubb at young age, getting her first taste of competitive skiing and showing an obvious talent.
In March 2019, Emma marked herself out as a young skier to watch when she won the U16 Slalom in the FIS Children's Cup and right after that tackled her first senior FIS events.

Ahead of the 2020 season, Emma made the major decision to relocate to Germany to be closer to the alpine skiing resorts for training and ski for the German Ski Association. She made her debut in the second tier Europa Cup the same year, scoring here first podium in slalom the following January.
Just a few weeks later Emma joined the German team at the FIS Alpine Skiing World Championships, where she was part of the bronze medal-winning squad in the team event.

In November 2021, as soon as she turned 18, Emma entered her first FIS World Cup event in Lech/Zürs, Austria, and a few months later got her first taste of Olympic competition in China. She was again part of the medal-winning German team, this time securing a silver medal, as well as winning a trio of silver medals at the 2022 Junior World Championships in slalom, giant slalom and downhill.

In February of 2025, Emma finished on the podium of a World Cup event for the first time in her career, taking second place in the downhill at Kvitfjell, Norway. The next day she upped her level once again, bringing home her first win from Saturday's downhill race in the same location.

It was to be her first of two wins inside a month, with the second coming two weeks later in the Super G at La Thuile, Italy. "I'm happy with how I've improved over the last few weeks. It was fun to ski," she said.

In 2026, Emma had the opportunity to compete at her second Winter Games and added to her medal collection. She won silver in the downhill event and two days later won another silver in the team combined slalom.
Consistently building her experience and speed on the world stage, it is clear Emma is going to be a name to contend with for years to come.

athletes.name: Eva Adamczyková
athletes.standfirst: A world champion in snowboard cross, Czech ace Eva Adamczyková has spent more than a decade at the very highest level of her sport.
bio: Hailing from Prague, Eva Adamczyková has been racing snowboard cross (SBX) competitively since 2008 and is seen as one of the greatest talents in Czech winter sports.

Having enjoyed a hugely successful junior career, becoming a world champion on three occasions, Eva effortlessly made the step up to elite level, becoming the 2013 Czech Republic National Champion and placing fourth overall in the 2013 World Cup rankings.

One year later she claimed a silver medal at the X Games and then won gold for her country in Sochi. It was not just Eva's incredible performances that caught the eye in Russia, with the Czech snowboard superstar competing with a fake moustache drawn on her face. “It's for luck,” she says. “I just want to have fun!”

Eva has continued to unleash a string of supreme performances on the monster-sized jumps and bumps of the SBX slope. In 2017 she was crowned the world champion and one year later claimed bronze in Pyeongchang.
2019 saw Eva land another world title, while in 2021 she dominated the World Cup, winning three of the season's six races to claim the overall title for a third time.

In late 2021, Eva suffered a career-threatening injury as she broke both of her ankles. Sidelined for 14 months, there were times when it seemed unlikely she would be able to return to competition. However, she made a triumphant return at the World Championships in Bakuriani, claiming gold in her first races post injury.
Having missed the 2022 Winter Games due to injury, Eva returned to the biggest stage at Milan-Cortina in 2026 and proved that she remains at the very top of her game as she claimed a silver medal.

athletes.name: Gee Atherton
athletes.standfirst: A multiple world champion, World Cup winner and Red Bull Rampage podium finisher, Gee Atherton is one of the greatest MTB riders of his generation.
bio: Known across the world of mountain biking as Gee, the middle Atherton sibling has been a sensation in the sport since the age of 15.

In 2004, at the age of 19, he won his first Downhill World Cup on the technically challenging track in the Austrian resort of Schladming. A win at this level may have seemed inevitable after his results in the junior categories, including two World Championship medals, but to gain it at such a young age was outstanding.

That year he also won the National Championships at his first attempt and went on to top podiums the world over, most notably taking gold at the 2008 World Championship alongside sister Rachel Atherton , and securing the 2010 Mountain Bike World Cup crown.
With second at Red Bull Rampage in 2004, the toughest of events to be judged on creativity rather than speed, he demonstrated his all-round talent.

Gee placed second at the end of the 2013 World Cup Series, and took the title as British downhill national champion 2013. He headed into 2014 even more focused and determined, the highlight of his season being the win at the World Championship in Hafjell. Gee tore into the World Cup competition in Cairns to take the win, but couldn’t find the pace for the podium in a tough field, ultimately finishing his 2014 World Cup season fifth overall.

Sadly 2017 followed in the same injury-plagued vein, with Gee suffering a dislocated hip, but as one of the fittest and most determined racers on the circuit, he didn't let that hold him back for long. He returned to action in 2018 and looked to be getting back to the sort of form he's known for towards the end of the season, signing off with a silver medal at the World Champs and taking the win at Red Bull Hardline.

The 2019 season saw Gee embark on a new venture with his very own Atherton Bikes brand alongside his sister, Rachel, where he raced and developed their new DH bike on the World Cup circuit, ending the year with another podium performance at the world's toughest downhill race, Red Bull Hardline, with a strong second place.
Filming his The Knife Edge video near Dinas Mawddwy, Wales, he broke his leg, wrist, ribs, nose and eye socket, as well as suffering concussion.
But far from putting him off from riding risky lines, Gee couldn't wait to get back to it as soon as possible:

"I can honestly say that being injured hasn’t put me off this kind of riding," he said. "In fact it’s the complete opposite. The thought of more of these challenges is the light at the end of the tunnel, the reason I’ve pushed on with physio so early, it’s what helps me face the daily grind of painful rehab.
"It's my goal. I’m passionate about the projects and I plan to do more as soon as I can."

Today, Gee is focused less on chasing World Cup titles and more on pushing the boundaries of mountain biking through pioneering film projects - such as the Ridgeline series - development at Atherton Bikes and the evolution of Red Bull Hardline .

athletes.name: Haley Adams
athletes.standfirst: Haley Adams is a former teenage champion and three-time top-five CrossFit Games finisher who has competed among functional fitness’s elite for nearly a decade.
bio: Haley Adams has spent a decade progressing through competitive functional fitness, from teenage podiums to top-five finishes in the elite women’s field. Along the way, she has built a career defined by both high-level consistency and a renewed perspective on competition.

After a background in gymnastics, Adams discovered CrossFit as a teenager and quickly showed she could compete with the best athletes in her age group. She finished second in the Girls 14–15 division in 2016 and again took runner-up in Girls 16–17 the following year.
In 2018, she completed that progression by winning the Girls 16–17 title, establishing herself as one of the leading young athletes in the sport before moving into the elite women’s field.

Adams made an immediate impact after stepping up to the elite women’s division, finishing sixth in 2019, fourth in 2020 and fifth in 2021. She followed that with ninth in 2022, completing four consecutive top-10 finishes, a consistency she has credited in part to working deliberately on areas that come less naturally to her, including heavy lifting.

In 2023, Adams took a year away from competition after experiencing burnout, struggling with what she described as “eating issues” and feeling she had missed out on simply living life after years of intense training and competition. Looking back, she says the decision proved transformative: “It ended up being one of the best things I've done because I had such an amazing year, truly. I was just so burnt out and needed a break.”

Adams returned to elite competition in 2024 and finished fifth, with qualifying again carrying special significance after her year away. “It was definitely one of the highlights of my career,” she says.
Adams has continued competing at the highest level since her comeback, remaining a regular presence among the sport’s elite.
Away from competition, Adams is a self-proclaimed Disney and Star Wars fan who has learned to place greater value on family, friendships and life outside the gym.

athletes.name: Hazim Ahmad
athletes.standfirst: The Malaysian freestyle soccer athlete has made a name for himself internationally, but his passion is building the sport in his home country.
bio: Hazim 'Zeem' Ahmad began learning freestyle soccer in 2006 at the age of 10 after witnessing a freestyle performance on the street and being amazed by the moves. He started catching more performances before seeking out Dr Freestyler Malaysia (Amy), one of the sport’s pioneers in Malaysia, for training.
After four years of training from Amy, he was able to master the sport's basics. Then he wanted to experiment with his skills and began to use YouTube to learn new and exciting tricks.
Zeem has helped to put Malaysia on the map when it comes to freestyle soccer. At the 2016 World Street Soccer Championship in Denmark, he was among the few Asian faces present.
He also represented Malaysia as a trainer at the Panna Home Training Camp 2019 in Japan, while in 2022 the team he coached triumphed at the Red Bull Neymar Jr’s Five World Final.

Extremely passionate about freestyle soccer, Zeem is helping the sport gain recognition in Malaysia and beyond. One of the ways he achieves this is through his One2one Academy, where he coaches young players to follow their passion for freestyle soccer.

athletes.name: Henrique Avancini
athletes.standfirst: World Cup-winning Brazilian cross-country rider Henrique Avancini puts his elite skills on a mountain bike down to his rural roots.
bio: Henrique Avancini was born and raised in Petrópolis, near Rio de Janeiro. He got his first bike at the age of eight, when his father, Ruy, recycled a large 22" broken bike frame, transforming it into a special size – 12.5" – just for his son.

Henrique quickly found his balance and, growing up in the countryside, was able to hone his MTB cross-country skills. With hard work and determination, the Brazilian became the first rider in his country to win the national championship in all categories, from junior through to elite level.

2017 was the year Henrique really started to make waves in the normally European-dominated XCO rankings, when he claimed his first World Cup top-10 finish in Andorra and finished an eye-catching fourth at the World Championships in Cairns, Australia, to end the year fifth in the UCI's rankings.

Henrique really kicked on from that result during the 2018 season, where he scored a first win in the new XC Short Track format and scored two podium finishes in the main XCO races during the World Cup season before winning the UCI XCM Marathon World Championships - his first world title – to end the season ranked as the second best cross country racer in the world behind the great Nino Schurter.

In 2019 he had another brilliant season, where he showed his incredible power to win and scored a run of top-three finishes in XCC, as well as claiming his first pair of third-place finishes in XCO, again ending the year ranked second overall by the UCI.

Still improving his riding and fitness every year, Henrique achieved his long-held goal of winning a UCI XCO World Cup race during the double-header 2020 World Cup weekend in Nové Město, where he timed his sprint to perfection to take a brilliant, emotional victory in the second full XCO race of the weekend.
In 2021, the UCI MTB World Championship started a new tradition of awarding medals for the XC Short Track race. Henrique clinched the silver medal, landing on the podium again.

In 2023, Henrique took on a new challenge as he led his own team – Caloi Henrique Avancini Racing Team – to head up an all-Brazilian team in World Cup racing for the very first time. That move soon paid off, with victory at the Glasgow edition of the UCI Mountain Bike World Championships.

At the end of 2023, a season in which Henrique triumphed at the UCI Mountain Bike XC Marathon World Championship, the Brazilian decided to call time on his cross-country racing career. However, it wouldn't be long before he was back in the saddle, and in 2025 he announced he would try racing on the road.
Now competing in events around the world, he secured his first major victory at the Brazilian Time Trial National Championship in the summer of 2026.

athletes.name: Igor Amorelli
athletes.standfirst: Brazilian triathlete Igor Amorelli regularly excels over long distances and is a consistent winner of high-profile Ironman events.
bio: In 2014, Igor Amorelli made a name for himself when he became the first Brazilian to win the Ironman Brazil title with a powerful performance in Florianopólis. Aside from the plaudits gained after his 8h 2m 54s victory, the triathlete was also rewarded with the energy and confidence required to keep focusing on the 3.8km swim, 180km bike and 42km run.

Besides the excellent performance at Florianópolis – aka Ilha da Magia – Igor also added three more podium finishes in 2014 – at the Ironman 70.3 races in Brasilia, Steel Head and Timberman, the last two of which are run in the US. The following year, again in Florianópolis, the athlete became the first South American to complete an Ironman race in under eight hours.

Like any triathlete, Amorelli recognises that he has strengths and weaknesses on the three different stages. "The goal is to be as complete as possible, but I feel better swimming and biking. Usually I need to be very good physically to be able to perform better in the race," he said.
Mineiro by birth, but with the southern-Brazilian state of Santa Catarina in his heart, Amorelli currently lives and trains in Baleário Camburiú.

athletes.name: iiTzTimmy
athletes.standfirst: From tactical shooters to the world of streaming, iiTzTimmy puts in the work to be the best.
bio: Video Games have always played a pivotal role in Timothy “iiTzTimmy” An’s life. iiTzTimmy’s initial love for gaming began at a very young age playing MapleStory with his brother, before shifting his focus to League of Legends and Soldier Front 2, where he would spend numerous hours grinding both games. It wasn’t long before that natural love for gaming turned into aspirations to make it his full-time career right around the start of Apex Legends. Since then, iiTzTimmy has become one of the most popular streamers on Twitch, amassing over 1 million Twitch followers within two months of streaming and hitting 163K concurrent viewers during his historic ‘Solo Bronze to Predator’ marathon stream.

A naturally charismatic and entertaining personality, iiTzTimmy has built a nest of devout followers who love tuning into his regularly scheduled streams. Yet, what sets iiTzTimmy apart from other entertainers stems from his other passion for competition.

As a pro Apex Legends competitor, iiTzTimmy has surpassed all expectations from the community following his return to the competitive scene in 2023 where his team, The Dojo, secured a surprise top-four finish at the ALGS: 2023 Championship.
Now, iiTzTimmy is looking to build upon his unique success as both a popular streamer and top esports competitor as he sets his sights on being a multi-faceted legend in gaming.

athletes.name: Jesse Augustinus
athletes.standfirst: No mountains is no problem for Jesse Augustinus, the Dutch rail master.
bio: At eight years of age Jesse Augustinus stood on a snowboard for the first time. Why? Because he was bored during the winter. Just as well really, because after he mastered the basics, he was always going to go on to do more in the snowboarding world.

First a rail here, a kicker there and then on to focus fully on slopestyle. These days he’s a familiar face on the international scene, competing in competitions like Burton Rail Days, Stairsmaster and Red Bull The Station, which he won in 2015, while in 2016 he topped the podium at DC Shred Fest. He’s also known for his killer urban edits.

athletes.name: Kaylea Arnett
athletes.standfirst: One of the most exciting newcomers to the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series in recent years, Kaylea Arnett followed up her dazzling debut season with another strong performance in 2025.
bio: After an impressive 4th place finish at the 2024 World Championships in Doha heralded a potential new challenger to the women’s elite, the Texas-born athlete announced herself on the World Series stage with two runner-up finishes at her first two stops that year; her dream debut coming on home soil in Boston.
It was clear that the women’s champion Rhiannan Iffland - who in recent years had only been challenged by Molly Carlson – now had a new serious contender to deal with.

Despite injury ending the 32-year-old’s chances of making a play for the title that season, Arnett's return to the 21 m platform in Montreal earned the American diver another podium finish, elevating her to an overall fifth-place finish – and scoring Arnett an invitation to permanent status for the 2025 season.

Last year, two more podiums followed, including another runner-up spot at the Philippines season opener. Despite those results being slightly offset by an underwhelming 11th place finish at the Boston finale, where she was fortunate to escape unscathed after making contact with the platform, Arnett managed to hold on for third place in the overall standings.

Having suffered mental and physical burnout during her years as a traditional diver, Arnett was initially hesitant to continue diving, fearing it could taint her love for the sport. But the lure of cliff diving was too great, and Arnett says her past experiences have made her stronger: “Now that I am a bit older and wiser, my goal is to simply enjoy each dive and embrace the experience.”

Ahead of the Boston competition last season, Arnett revealed the philosophy behind her style and success out on the platform: “I told myself if I’m going to do this sport, I’m not going to do it the way the old Kaylea would. I’m going to be a performer rather than a competitor, and that’s how I’ll keep it fun and fresh.” Watch Arnett open up about her deeply emotional past, her ethos, and what drives in her in Will They Crack Under Pressure?
As for 2026, if the vibrant and super-energetic American diver can stay fit and focused, then reigning champion Iffland will certainly have a title fight on her hands...
2025 - 3rd Place Overall: Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series
2024 - 3rd Place: World Aquatics World Cup - Manama, Bahrain

athletes.name: Kyohei Arata
athletes.standfirst: The first-ever Japanese representative at the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series, Kyohei Arata, will make his debut on home soil in 2023.
bio: Takachiho, in Miyazaki Prefecture, is the stunning location where the 27-year-old wildcard gets to show off his high diving skills for the very first time in competition.

A 10m synchro winner at the 2017 Japan Championships, the diving coach from Takoaka describes the moment that he first leaped from 27m at the AREA 47 training pool in Austria as the best moment of his career so far. His goal for this season is to hit high scores and stay injury-free.

athletes.name: Luc Ackermann
athletes.standfirst: One of the most innovative freestyle motocross riders around, Luc Ackermann collects world records for fun and scored a big X Games title in 2021.
bio: FMX is not the sport of an average guy, but Luc Ackermann is definitely anything but average. Not only was the German the youngest athlete ever to perform a backflip on a motorbike, but he’s also considered as one of the biggest talents in FMX.
But Ackermann doesn’t rest on his laurels. Ever. He just keeps pushing himself to the next level. He handles his bike like an old pro, and is learning new and harder tricks all the time.

In 2013, he joined the legendary Travis Pastrana on his Nitro Circus Germany Tour, and fans can also catch Ackermann in action at the Night of the Jumps tour, where he’s scored a string of podium finishes.
In 2014 at just 16 years of age he achieved the best ever finish at a Red Bull X-Fighters event by a German rider when he finished fourth in Munich.

In 2017 Luc landed the "youngest motorcycle double backflip of all time", reaching another World Record at the age of 19, then a year later in 2018 he became the youngest FIM European FMX Champion at Night of the Jumps.
Another big breakthrough came in 2021 with FMX victories at the X Games in Encinitas, California. Luc would also take first place at Night Of The Jumps, a title he successfully defended in 2022.

In the past few years, Luc has continued to lead the progression of freestyle motocross. In 2025, he won the Night of the Jumps World Tour Championship and garnered more worldwide attention with his Red Bull Tsunami backflip between two moving trucks. In 2026, he set his 14th world record by becoming the first rider to land a double backflip over an obstacle at Le Mans.

athletes.name: Luc Alphand
athletes.standfirst: A master of two sports, Luc Alphand had a successful career as a skier before making the move into motorsport and becoming a world-renowned rally driver.
bio: As a skier, Luc Alphand began with a Junior World Downhill title in 1983 and has a superb domestic record, having claimed eight French downhill championships throughout the ’80s and ’90s, the Combined title in 1987 and the Super-G title in 1988.
On the international stage, Luc won the World Cup downhill titles in 1995, 1996 and 1997, with the latter year also seeing him take the Super-G and Overall World Cup crowns.

He first competed in motorsport in the late 1990s, driving for the first time in the legendary Dakar Rally in 1998. He won his first event, the World Cup T1 Marathon, in a Mitsubishi Pajero in 1999. After a number of impressive results throughout the years, Luc achieved the big one by winning the Dakar in 2006, again in a trusted Mitsubishi.
No stranger to the track either, Luc has competed with great success in the Porsche Carrera Cup and the Le Mans 24 Hours Race, where he has achieved podium spots three times in a Chevrolet Corvette.

After suffering a back injury in an accident in 2009, he has now retired from competitive racing. As a nod to Alphand’s skiing origins, a black ski run at the resort of Chantemerle, near to his hometown of Briançon, is named in his honour.

athletes.name: Ludwig Ahgren
athletes.standfirst: One of the biggest names in livestreaming and esports, Ludwig is a charismatic creator, multi-record setting gamer, and entertainer.
bio: Ludwig’s personality, charisma, and ability to entertain has helped him become one of the largest and most influential content creators in the gaming industry today.

Ludwig began streaming in 2018, but he really started to gain attention when he broke the button mashing world record for Mario Party 4 in 2019. He quickly followed this achievement by accumulating over 1 million followers on both Twitch and YouTube in 2020.

Since then, Ludwig has continued to scale up to become one of the biggest streamers in the world as he set new sub world records across Twitch and won various gaming industry awards and streamer accolades, including Content Creator of the Year at the Game Awards 2022.
Ludwig is continuing to evolve his content, as he focuses on collaborating with other top gaming creators and producing large-scale events and stunts that push the boundaries of the gaming world.

athletes.name: Luke Aikins
athletes.standfirst: Breaking boundaries is second nature to American skydiver and pilot Luke Aikins.
bio: Luke has been pushing the bounds of human flight for more than 28 years and is an acclaimed skydiver, commercial airplane and helicopter pilot, film stuntman, innovator and coach. While he has more than 21,000 skydives and 8,750 flight hours, his main purpose is constant professional growth and aiding in the development of others to leverage their full potential.

Aviation is in Luke’s blood. He was surrounded by a family full of pilots and skydivers and raised on a private airport where his grandfather founded a skydiving center in the ‘60s after returning from the war as a P-47 pilot. In fact, Luke made his first skydive and earned his pilot’s license at age 16.

With an ongoing desire to advance the industry, Luke devotes much of his time to research and development of equipment and flying techniques. The skilled skydiver lent his expertise and skillset to developing technologically advanced systems for the highly publicized Red Bull Stratos mission in 2012. He designed, built, and tested the equipment used for the project that saw Felix Baumgartner successfully jump from 128,000 feet. Luke also invented a one-of-a-kind device that deployed parachutes and drogue chutes based on the G-forces and time of exposure.

In addition to innovation and performing demonstrations globally with the Red Bull Air Force, Luke trains celebrities and military personnel with cutting-edge skydiving techniques while also acting as a Hollywood stuntman. He has coordinated scenes in blockbusters such as Iron Man 3, Godzilla, the Fast and Furious franchise, Ant-Man 2 and more. He has also served as aerial photographer and cinematographer for some of these productions.

On top of Luke’s already impressive list of accomplishments is a historic record-breaking jump on live TV where he intentionally dove from 25,000 feet with no parachute, successfully landing within a 100ft. x 100ft. specially designed net. Luke also concepted and oversaw Red Bull Aces, a four-cross head-to-head wingsuit slalom race.

Today, Luke and his cousin and fellow Red Bull Air Force teammate Andy Farrington share a 40-acre property in Washington with an airplane hangar and grass runway where they are raising their children the same way they were raised: flying and skydiving.

athletes.name: Madars Apse
athletes.standfirst: One of Latvia's most well-known athletes, Madars Apse is much-loved and respected around the world as a skater and community advocate.
bio: Latvian skateboarder extraordinaire Madars Apse has practically been surgically attached to his skateboard since 2001.
The Ventspils native has made quite a name for himself throughout Europe and on the global scene during his time on the circuit, winning national and international contests and travelling the world.

Arguably the hottest property in street skating today, he broke the United States' historical resistance to foreign upstarts by putting out a frankly ridiculous run of video parts on both sides of the Atlantic.

Athletic, creative, spontaneous and super-stylish for a big guy, Madars became really good very quickly and then, where lesser talents peaked, he stayed on that rocket ride where he was better at the end of a session than he was at the start.
Magazine covers and accolades galore haven't swayed his sense of self as the charming, cerebral and witty upstart that everyone in the international skate scene knows and loves.

Madars is big on giving back to his native Latvian scene both through DIY park projects and by using his international status to hold the door open for more talent to come through out of the Baltic state he still calls home.
In 2020, Madars debuted series one of his show Skate Tales , which became the biggest online skate series in the world in just its first season alone.

Skate Tales returned to the screens of skateboarders the world over in 2022, as Madars once again took us all on a journey around skateboarding’s outside edge – from freestyling models to Ugandan skatepark pioneers. With a new season being released year after year the show has grown into the biggest skateboarding series on the internet.
His trailblazing signature show has positioned Madars right at the top of the skateboarding scene and cements his status as one of the world’s favourite skateboarders.

Madars continues to be a major competitive and inspirational face and force on the international skateboarding scene year after year, showing his skill at events such as Red Bull Steep Street in Prague, Dime Glory Challenge in Montreal, and KASSO FEST Skate & Sound obstacle course in Japan and California.

athletes.name: Mansour Al Safran
athletes.standfirst: The former kayaker always had a passion for two-wheels and after switching sports became the first Kuwaiti pro BMX rider.
bio: Kuwaiti BMX rider Mansour Al Safran is one of the top sportsmen in his region. He began his career as a flat-water kayaker, competing for four years and earning a place in the Kuwait national team, but he couldn’t hold back his passion for BMX.

He made the switch to BMX Freestyle in 2006, making his national debut at the Red Bull Street Style event in Kuwait City the same year. His dream was always to go pro – in his early BMX days, Mansour watched his idols and pro freestyle athletes, learning from the best. He picked up tricks, whips and the skills that saw him ultimately achieve his goal of becoming the first Kuwaiti pro BMX rider.

His easy, flowing style has earned him a number of top spots in regional competitions. A bronze medal at a 2013 Asian freestyle tournament in Malaysia was a pivotal moment for the Kuwaiti athlete, as he shredded his way onto the international scene to compete alongside the best.

athletes.name: Melita Abraham
athletes.standfirst: Part of a family dynasty of rowers in her native Chile, picking up medals and growing her reputation one competition at a time.
athletes.discipline: Rowing Quadruple Sculls / Rowing Light Weight / Rowing Pairs
bio: Melita Abraham and her siblings are putting Chilean rowing on the map with impressive performances at international competitions. Melita is one of four quadruplets and competes alongside her sister Antonia, while her brothers Ignacio and Alfredo also represent their country on the world stage.

Melita and her siblings started rowing thanks to a chance invitation from a friend of their brother Ignacio. While still in primary school, Melita first went along to the lakes of the Regatta Club in Concepción, near her family home in San Pedro de la Paz. It was the first step on a path that's taking her around the world with her oars in hand.

Outstanding performances at the 2018 South American Games saw Melita take LW1x gold on her own plus further golds in the W4x, W2x and the W2- competitions with Melita. There have also been encouraging results in Europe, including silver at the Rowing World Cup, plus a slew of Pan-American Games medals of every colour.

athletes.name: Saul Leonardo 'MenaRD' Mena Segundo
athletes.standfirst: Hailing from the Dominican Republic, MenaRD has already cemented himself as a legend of Street Fighter because of his natural talents for the game.
bio: “The embodiment of the perfect player,” Red Bull Kumite commentator Michael “Yipes” Mendoza stated when asked about Saul Leonardo “MenaRD” Mena Segundo.

Perfect is a word that seldomly gets thrown around in competitive gaming because of the volatility that naturally follows Street Fighter. However, no other player other than “The Strongest Bull” himself can call themselves a two-time Capcom Cup champion. Hailing from the Dominican Republic, MenaRD has already cemented himself as a legend of Street Fighter because of his natural talents for the game. Yet, what separates MenaRD from his fellow competitors is his unwavered loyalty and commitment to his Dominican roots.

As the first Latin-American player to hoist the Capcom Cup, MenaRD used his $250,000 winnings to fund more support towards the Dominican fighting game scene and esports communities before winning yet another Capcom Cup, as well as Red Bull Kumite and Evo Japan 2024.
“What I love about Mena is that he never changes as a person,” Yipes said about MenaRD. “Everyone that roots for him sees a piece of themselves in Mena.”

As one of Street Fighter’s brightest talents, “The Strongest Bull” has already etched himself in the Street Fighter history books as a generational talent. The only question left is what’s next in his ongoing quest to continue pushing himself and the Dominican Republic forward.

athletes.name: Mosaad Al Dossary
athletes.standfirst: Saudi Arabia's Musaed 'Msdossary' Al Dossary is widely recognised as one of the most accomplished FIFA players in the world.
bio: Saudi Arabia's Musaed 'Msdossary' Al Dossary really exploded onto the international FIFA scene in 2018.

The Saudi Arabian player has since done just about all there is to do in the FIFA scene and his most notable titles include his win in the FIFA eWorld Cup Grand Final and taking home the Esports Player of the Year Award, but there's plenty more besides.

Like so many young boys, Msdossary dreamed of becoming a footballer when he was growing up, but while that ambition didn't pan out, his digital football career certainly has. "I always loved to play football and at some time, I wished that I would become a pro and play football, but my career in FIFA is good so I’m happy with it," he says.
The three-time FUT Champions Cup winner is the first Saudi electric league winner and is the only person in history to have won back-to-back XBox World Championships in FIFA's history.

He also looked well on course to win a second FIFA eWorld Cup in 2020, after producing some blistering displays in early tournaments before the FIFA pro scene was put on hold, but Msdossary will be ready to play for more titles for years to come, almost certainly playing teams featuring his two go-to football legends, Cristiano Ronaldo and Ruud Gullit.
Following all of this FIFA success, Msdossary has even been invited to personally meet the King of Saudi Arabia.

athletes.name: Nasser Al Attiyah
athletes.standfirst: Nasser Al-Attiyah is the sporting hero of his native Qatar who's won the Dakar Rally on six occasions while also excelling in skeet shooting.
bio: Nasser Al-Attiyah is an extremely talented rally driver and skeet shooter who’s always motivated to stay on top of his game. A six-time winner of the Dakar Rally and a bronze medallist in shooting, he’s now considered an icon of Qatari sports.
Nasser’s rise to glory at the Dakar Rally has been astonishing. He finished second in 2010 – just 2m 12s behind Carlos Sainz, which is still the narrowest margin in the history of the race.

A year later he went one better and won the competition, becoming the first Arab to do so. But that wasn’t enough, and he secured a second Dakar title in style, dominating the 2015 edition of the toughest rally-raid event from start to finish in a Mini.

More success came in 2015 for the Qatari speedster and his French co-driver Mathieu Baumel as they won the FIA Cross-Country Rally World Cup. The duo then switched to a Toyota in 2017 and two years later delivered the Japanese brand their first Dakar win.

Nasser once again showed blistering form throughout the 2021 FIA World Cup for Cross-Country-Rallies and started 2022 with a bang. Racing the new-look Toyota Hilux T1+ model at the Dakar Rally, he dominated his rivals to win his fourth title and first in Saudi Arabia.

His stellar start to 2022 turned into a brilliant summer as well, as Nasser took on some of his biggest rally-raid rivals in the inaugural FIA World Rally-Raid Championship, which he won over Sébastien Loeb in thrilling final showdown at the Andalucia Rally.
Nasser successfully defended his Dakar title in 2023 with Toyota Gazoo Racing, as he took his fifth driver's title in Saudi Arabia.

His bid to become the first driver to win the Dakar Rally with four different manufacturers ended in disappointment in 2024 as he was forced to walk away from his malfunctioning Prodrive Hunter vehicle.

In 2025, he joined the all-new Dacia Sandriders Team in a powerhouse squad alongside Sébastien Leob and Cristina Gutiérrez . He enjoyed immediate success, winning the punishing Rallye du Maroc in his first outing in the car. He then narrowly missed out on a podium finish at the Dakar, finishing in fourth place.
The following year, Nasser secured his historic sixth overall Dakar Rally car title, setting a record by becoming the first driver to win with four different manufacturers.
"We've worked very hard since last year. I might not be showing much emotion yet, but it's there, deep down. We are so happy to win," he said at the finish.

athletes.name: Olivia Babcock
athletes.standfirst: University of Pittsburgh All-American standout who is an emerging star in women’s volleyball.
bio: After Olivia Babcock’s freshman season at University of Pittsburgh, she earned the accolade of not only AVCA Freshman of the Year but also AVCA First-Time All American. She did not fully comprehend this feat until her teammate pointed out how rare it is for a freshman.
The talent that Olivia has is propelling her to the top of women’s volleyball, but it was one discovered late.

Growing up in Los Angeles, California, Olivia enjoyed playing all sports, primarily focusing on soccer and water polo. It wasn’t until she started playing beach volleyball with her sister when she realized the unlocked potential she had and the love for the game.

“I really liked a lot of the other sports I played, but it was very clear to me that I was only doing it to stay in shape,” Olivia said. “But then when I started playing volleyball, I was like, ‘Oh, wait. I want to be in the gym. I want to get better.’”

In her junior season for Pittsburgh Panthers in 2025, Olivia set a program record with 41 kills against Louisville and broke it two weeks later with 45 against North Carolina. She earned AVCA Player of the Week once and ACC Offensive Player of the Week five times.

She repeated as ACC Player of the Year – the first in program history to do so – and repeated as AVCA National Player of the Year, becoming the fifth player to win it in consecutive seasons. She also received the inaugural AVCA Rightside Hitter of the Year award and again won the Honda Sports Award for volleyball.
She led the Panthers to a fifth straight national semi-final, where they were swept by eventual champions Texas A&M, finishing with a match-high 22 kills and six blocks.

In addition to her collegiate accolades, Olivia has represented the United States on the international stage. She was part of the team that won gold at the 2023 Girls U19 Pan American Cup, showcasing her ability to compete and excel against top global competition. In 2024, she continued to represent her country with pride, earning a silver medal at the NORCECA Women's Pan American Cup Final Six.
She was one of only two active NCAA volleyball players selected to the United States Senior National Team for the 2025 Volleyball Nations League, where the team placed sixth.

Olivia Babcock’s combination of size, power, and court awareness has cemented her as one of the top rising stars in volleyball. As she continues her career at the University of Pittsburgh, fans and analysts alike are eager to see how she will further shape the future of the sport, both at the collegiate and international levels.

athletes.name: Pedro Acosta
athletes.standfirst: Spain's Pedro Acosta is a Red Bull MotoGP Rookies Cup, Moto3™ and Moto2™ champion and a MotoGP™ Sprint winner with Red Bull KTM Factory Racing.
bio: Pedro Acosta’s first experience of motorbikes came at the age of just five, when his father bought a motocross bike – and he hasn’t looked back since.
Having begun racing bikes at a young age, Acosta worked his way up through Minibikes, MiniGP, MaxxiGP and PreMoto3 before stepping into the Moto3™ Junior World Championship in 2018.

After one season in the juniors, Acosta, who lists Casey Stoner and Kevin Schwantz among his racing heroes, stepped up to the Red Bull Rookies Cup . He finished runner-up in 2019 before claiming the title the following season.

Acosta stepped up to Moto3™ with Red Bull KTM Ajo in 2021 and made an immediate impact. After finishing runner-up on his Grand Prix debut in Qatar, he won from the pit lane at the Doha Grand Prix in only his second race before taking another victory in Portimão at the following round.

The Doha victory made Acosta the first rider to win a Moto3™ Grand Prix from a pit-lane start. He continued to rewrite the record books throughout the season, eventually sealing the title in Portugal. Acosta became the first rookie to win the lightweight-class crown since Loris Capirossi in 1990 and, at 17 years and 166 days old, was the second-youngest Grand Prix world champion in history.
After his dominant Moto3™ rookie season, Acosta stepped up to Moto2™ with Red Bull KTM Ajo in 2022. He won three races, finished fifth overall and earned Moto2™ Rookie of the Year honours.

In 2023, Acosta dominated his second Moto2™ season with Red Bull KTM Ajo, taking seven wins and 14 podiums. He secured the title with two races remaining, becoming the youngest Moto2™ world champion in history.

After winning two world titles in three seasons, Acosta stepped up to MotoGP™ with Red Bull GASGAS Tech3 in 2024 and immediately established himself as one of the standout rookies of the premier class.

Acosta took two podiums in his first three MotoGP™ races, then added three more later in the year to finish the season with five Grand Prix podiums in total. He finished sixth overall and earned Rookie of the Year honours.
Acosta joined Red Bull KTM Factory Racing for 2025, adding five Grand Prix podiums and climbing to fourth in the MotoGP™ World Championship standings.

In 2026, Acosta claimed his first MotoGP™ Sprint victory in Thailand and added Grand Prix podiums in Thailand, the United States, Hungary and Aragón. With three runner-up finishes among those results, he continues to chase his first MotoGP™ Grand Prix victory.

athletes.name: Rachel Atherton
athletes.standfirst: With a record number of overall World Cup wins and the only perfect season in MTB history to her name, Rachel Atherton is the queen of downhill racing.
bio: Over the years, Rachel Atherton has become the dominant force in women's downhill racing. After winning a host of categories in 2005, she was named Times Young Sportswoman of the Year and hasn’t looked back since.

She totally commanded the women’s downhill circuit in 2008, winning the World Cup overall and taking World Championship gold. On her way to the World Cup overall she took four World Cup wins and only missed out on a top-two finish at one race, in Fort William.

Since 2008, she has won six UCI World Cup titles (2008, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2016 and 2018) and five World Champion titles (2008, 2013, 2015, 2016 and 2018). Only illness or injury has denied her the chance to compete at the top end of the sport, but she has always returned stronger.

Following illness in 2014, she bounced back to redefine women’s DH racing, doing the ‘double double’ in 2015 and 2016, and completing an unprecedented perfect season in 2016 by winning every World Cup round.

2018 saw her take a record sixth World Cup overall, before capping the season off with a fifth World Championship, thus reconfirming her place as the best female downhill mountain biker on the planet.
