The 2019 season was a mixed one for Rachel, with a strong start to the World Cup season cut short by a serious achilles rupture sustained in Les Gets. However, it also saw the successful launch of her very own Atherton Bikes brand alongside her brother, Gee.

Following the birth of her first child in 2021, Rachel made a long-awaited but surprise return to racing at the 2022 Lenzerheide World Cup in Switzerland, where she only narrowly missed a stunning podium finish.

But in 2023, she returned to top form at Lenzerheide and wrapped up her 40th UCI MTB World Cup win in brilliant fashion. You can see how Rachel balances motherhood and competitive racing in the video below.

athletes.name: Red Bull Blanix Aerobatic Team
athletes.standfirst: Red Bull Blanix Aerobatic Team
bio: It doesn't have to be fast and noisy to be thrilling – one display by the Red Bull Blanix Aerobatic Team will prove that to you. Picture a pair of silent gliders, one of them in inverted flight, the other immediately below with barely a wingspan separating them, flying in perfect mirror flight. It's a very aeronautically demanding formation for powerless gliders, but that's exactly why Red Bull Blanix Aerobatic Team shows are so impressive.

Performances by the team not only includes classic aerobatics in addition to the mirror flight, but the show is supported by music as well as smoke and light effects on the gliders' wingtips, delivering something that's part aerial display, part concert.

The team's Blanik L13 glider is perfect for formation flight thanks to its beautiful, flowing flight silhouette and low flight speed capabilities. The two planes, which were built in 1965 and 1972 respectively, might well be 'vintage' but are in excellent condition and perfect for the job at hand, not least thanks to their solid metal construction.

Thanks to a unique flaps design, the Blanik L13 can land at very short distances, which means it's not just big airfield shows where the Red Bull Blanix Aerobatic Team can wow audiences in some very different location. So far that's included on the infamously steep slopes of Austria's legendary Hahnenkamm downhill ski course, golf courses or in front of Vienna's Donauturm Tower landmark.

In addition to the classic flight shows, Red Bull Blanix Aerobatic Team has also teamed up with the Red Bull Skydive Team to form Akte BlaniX 1 bis 3, where man and machine become connected and joint flight ideas previously not thought possible have been implemented in spectacular fashion.

athletes.name: Rhys McClenaghan
athletes.standfirst: An artistic gymnast from Northern Ireland specialising in the pommel horse, Rhys McClenaghan is an Olympic champion, two-time world champion and three-time European champion.
bio: From a young age, Northern Ireland’s Rhys McClenaghan showed an affinity for gymnastics. He began training at the age of six, excelled on the junior circuit and successfully transitioned to the senior ranks.

While still a junior, he won bronze on the pommel horse at the 2016 British Artistic Gymnastics Championships before earning silver at the Junior European Championships. The result was Ireland’s first-ever European gymnastics medal.

At the 2018 Commonwealth Games on Australia’s Gold Coast, McClenaghan won pommel horse gold, beating reigning world and Olympic champion Max Whitlock on execution after the pair finished level on 15.100.

Over the following years, McClenaghan continued to make history for Irish gymnastics. He claimed bronze at the 2019 World Championships, becoming the first Irish gymnast to win a world medal, before taking consecutive world titles in 2022 and 2023. He also won Commonwealth silver in 2022 and added European titles in 2023 and 2024, taking his continental tally to three.

In 2024, McClenaghan added the one major medal missing from his collection by winning pommel horse gold at the Paris Games with a score of 15.533. The result delivered Ireland’s first-ever Olympic gymnastics medal and made him the first gymnast to hold Olympic, world, European and Commonwealth titles on the same apparatus.

After shoulder surgery delayed his return to competition, McClenaghan made a winning comeback in March 2026, taking pommel horse gold at the Antalya World Cup. Later that year, he reached his third Commonwealth Games pommel horse final in Glasgow, finishing sixth.

athletes.name: Rokas Baciuška
athletes.standfirst: From European Rallycross champion to Dakar winner, Lithuania's Rokas Baciuška has become one of motorsport's most versatile stars.
bio: Rokas Baciuška is proud to be the first Lithuanian to compete in the World Rallycross Championship (2019), as well as the youngest Lithuanian to compete at the Dakar Rally (2022).

Rokas began racing karts at the age of nine and quickly established himself as one of the fastest young drivers in the Baltic region. In his final karting season in 2017, he finished seventh in the CIK-FIA Karting KZ2 European Championship and 14th in the CIK-FIA Karting KZ2 World Championship.
At 18, Rokas made his European Rallycross Championship debut in the Super1600 category and won the title in his rookie season.

He switched to rally raid in 2021, recording impressive results including fourth at the Andalucía Rally and fifth at Rallye du Maroc. The following year, he made his FIA World Rally-Raid Championship debut, finishing runner-up at the Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge and Andalucía Rally, winning Rallye du Maroc and securing the 2022 FIA T4 World Championship.

Rokas also made his Dakar Rally debut in 2022, finishing third in the SSV class and earning Rookie of the Year honours. He returned in 2023, winning three stages before mechanical problems ended his bid for victory, although he still finished second overall in the T4 category with the Red Bull Can-Am Factory Team.

He successfully defended the SSV title in 2023 before moving to Challenger and winning that championship in 2024, becoming the first W2RC driver to win world titles in two different categories. He finished Dakar 2024 third place overall in the T3 class, before victories at BP Ultimate Rally-Raid Portugal and Desafio Ruta 40 highlighted another impressive campaign.

In 2025, Rokas graduated to the ultimate car category at the Dakar Rally. Mechanical problems on the opening stage cost him more than two hours, but he bounced back immediately to claim his first career stage victory in the premier car class.
Rokas reached another milestone in 2026 when he claimed a dominant victory in the Dakar Rally's Stock class with Defender Rally, winning multiple stages to secure his first Dakar title.

Later in the year, he returned to his rallycross roots by rejoining the FIA European Rallycross Championship in the premier RX1 class, adding another exciting chapter to the career of one of Lithuania's most accomplished motorsport stars.

athletes.name: Romain Allemand
athletes.standfirst: Romain Allemand is a talented and creative freestyle snowboarder at the forefront of the French new wave.
bio: Hailing from Marseille, France, Romain Allemand represents the new wave of French freestyle snowboarding. A proud member of the French national snowboard team, he’s already making a name for himself with a style that blends creativity, amplitude and contagious good vibes.

From his very first runs, Romain fell in love with the freedom of freestyle. What drives him is turning every feature into a playground, every jump into a chance to express himself - constantly pushing his own limits. His aerial flow and knack for inventing new tricks make him stand out as a rider known for both his boldness and his positive energy.

In March 2024, he made history by earning his first-ever World Cup podium in Slopestyle at Tignes - a milestone for French snowboarding. A few months later, he backed it up with a third place in big air at Chur, before coming heartbreakingly close again at the 2025 World Championships in St Moritz, finishing fourth in both slopestyle and big air.

Continuing to carve his own line in the world of freestyle snowboarding, the teenager made the perfect start to 2026 by claiming victory in the slopestyle final at the Laax Open to become the first-ever French rider to win the event.

athletes.name: Ronnie
athletes.standfirst: Since 2004, breaker Ronnie Abaldonado has traveled the world battling, producing shows in his hometown, Las Vegas, running a hip-hop culture centre and being a Red Bull BC One All Star.
bio: Ronnie grew up in Guam, copying MTV dance moves. In 1993, he moved to California where his cousins taught him about breaking, hip-hop culture, and the foundations of the dance.

Ronnie credits his brother and B-Boy Ivan for his start in breaking. Ivan mentored Ronnie when he moved to Las Vegas to train with Full Force. Today, Ronnie is still a member of Full Force, Full Force Crew, Super Cr3w, and the Red Bull BC One All Stars.

With Super Cr3w, Ronnie won the 2008 season of "America’s Best Dance Crew." The win brought Ronnie and his crew massive mainstream recognition, and since then, Super Cr3w has performed at major events, including at the White House in 2010. Ronnie is also one of the first breakers to get a major sponsorship deal, continually building a multi-layered career as a competitive b-boy and dancer.

With his signature threads and freezes, Ronnie won the 2007 Red Bull BC One World Final in South Africa, a monumental win that was also documented in Turn it Loose. In 2000, Ronnie and Full Force won the Las Vegas Concrete Soul competition, defeating the legendary Texas Havikoro crew. Ronnie also won the 2016 UK B-Boy Championships crew battle with Red Bull BC One All Stars – a big moment for him after years of wanting to compete at the event.

Ronnie has put his heart and soul into dance. He’s the co-owner of Distrct Arts, his dance studio in Las Vegas, where he’s driven to continue building for the next generation of dancers. He organizes events and over the years, has put on qualification battles for the UK B-Boy Championships, R16 in South Korea, Battle of the Year, and Freestyle Sessions in California. Ronnie also wants to have longevity as a competitive B-Boy, break boundaries and set even more standards in breaking.

athletes.name: Elquaria
athletes.standfirst: With tens of thousands of followers and consistent viewership, Elquaria stands out in the German-language streaming scene as a creator who mixes fun, community engagement and personal flair.
bio: Sam 'Elquaria' is a German-speaking Twitch streamer based in Switzerland who has built a dedicated community around her entertaining mix of gaming and just-chatting livestreams.
In her streams, she embraces a personal, chat-friendly vibe. She has claimed that "Witcher 3 is the best game".

Beyond gaming, she emphasises authenticity, cross-platform presence and smart streaming practices – as she’s shared advice on finding one’s niche, choosing the right slot and not relying solely on one platform.

athletes.name: Sky Brown
athletes.standfirst: Sky Brown is a two-time Olympic medallist and world champion whose fearless skateboarding, remarkable comeback story and positive attitude inspire millions worldwide.
bio: Sky Brown is a British skateboarder and surfer who has become one of the most influential young athletes in the world. Born in Miyazaki, Japan, Brown competes internationally for Great Britain and is best known for her achievements in park skateboarding .

She rose to global prominence as a young skate phenom whose fearless style, positive attitude and remarkable talent captured the attention of fans around the world. She made history at Tokyo 2020 by winning bronze in the women's park event, becoming Great Britain's youngest-ever Olympic medallist.

Since then, she's built on that achievement with a second Olympic bronze medal at Paris 2024, while also becoming a two-time park world champion at the World Skateboarding Championships in 2023 and 2025.
Today, Brown is steadily becoming one of the biggest stars in skateboarding , inspiring the upcoming generations through her performances, personality and skill on a board.

Born and raised in Miyazaki, a coastal city on Japan's southern island of Kyushu, Brown grew up in a family that encouraged creativity, adventure and outdoor activities. Her father is British, while her mother is Japanese, giving her a multicultural upbringing that has shaped both her identity and outlook.

Sport was a natural part of everyday life for the young Browns. She spent her childhood surfing, skating and testing herself outdoors alongside her younger brother, Ocean, who has also developed into a talented skateboarder and surfer.
Much of her progression was self-taught, learned by watching older riders and constantly challenging herself.

Brown first stepped on a skateboard when she was just three years old. Growing up near beaches, with a skate ramp in her garden and a skate park at her preschool, she was exposed to both skateboarding and surfing from an early age and quickly developed a love for action sports.

Without formal coaching, she learned through observation and repetition, spending countless hours practising new tricks and riding increasingly challenging terrain. Her confidence and willingness to attempt difficult lines immediately set her apart from riders her age.

As videos of her skating began to circulate online, Brown attracted international attention for her ability to ride large ramps and bowls with a level of composure rarely seen in such a young athlete. Her progression was rapid, and at eight years old, she became the youngest rider to compete at the Vans US Open.

Although that initial appearance ended when she fell off her board during the heats, she became a regular competitor on the international circuit and quickly established herself as one of skateboarding's most exciting young talents.

In 2018, at the age of 10 she made history by turning pro and becoming the youngest professional skateboarder in the world. The following year she became the youngest-ever Nike-sponsored athlete. Around the same time, she began to emerge as a serious contender for Olympic qualification.

As skateboarding prepared to make its Olympic debut, Brown was becoming one of the young faces of the sport. Her combination of technical ability, creativity and fearlessness helped introduce millions of new fans to park skateboarding.
One of the defining moments of Brown's career came in 2020 when she suffered a life-threatening training accident while practising on a vert ramp in California.

The crash left her with multiple skull fractures, a broken left wrist and injuries to her hand and lungs. For a period, there were serious concerns about her recovery and whether she would be able to compete again at the highest level.

Brown approached rehabilitation with the same determination she showed on her skateboard. Within months, she was back on a board and gradually rebuilding her confidence. Her recovery became one of the most inspiring stories in sport, demonstrating extraordinary resilience for an athlete still in her early teens.

The comeback reached its perfect conclusion when she qualified for the Tokyo Olympics less than a year after the accident, turning a potentially career-limiting setback into one of the defining chapters of her journey.

The delayed Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games represented a landmark moment for both Brown and skateboarding. As the sport made its Olympic debut, Brown arrived as an athlete with her star on the rise, having won X Games gold the previous month.

Competing in the women's park event, she fell on both of her first two runs, before pulling out enough in her final attempt to secure the bronze medal. At just 13 years old, she became the youngest medallist in British Olympic history and one of the breakout stars of the Games.

Paris 2024 presented Brown with an opportunity to build on her Olympic skateboarding success. Entering the Games as one of the favourites, she once again demonstrated her ability to perform under pressure by securing a second consecutive Olympic bronze medal.

Away from skateboarding, she also publicly stated her ambition to compete at the highest level in surfing. While balancing two demanding sports presents a unique challenge, Brown was undaunted. She competed in the 2024 ISA World Surfing Games in Puerto Rico, where she placed 17th; the best result of any British surfer, but ultimately not enough for Olympic qualification.
Dig a little deeper into Sky Brown's surf side in Now Days:
Despite her young age, Brown has already compiled an extraordinary list of achievements.
Olympic bronze medallist in women's park skateboarding at Tokyo 2020
Many athletes achieve success through talent alone. Brown's influence comes from a rare combination of skill, resilience and authenticity.
Her willingness to compete across both skateboarding and surfing sets her apart from most elite athletes, while her fearless riding style continues to push progression in women's park skateboarding.

Equally important is her ability to connect with people to inspire the next generation. How many other big names have published a beginner's guide to skateboarding (check out The Life-Changing Magic of Skateboarding ). Brown's positivity, openness and enthusiasm have made her a role model for young skaters and surfers around the world.

Whether she's dropping into an intimidating bowl, competing at the pinnacle of her sport, pushing herself through injury or speaking from the heart to her millions of followers, her famous motto perfectly sums it up: "Be brave, have fun and do it 'cause you love it!"

athletes.name: Sofia 'SofiKimmy' Aravena
athletes.standfirst: Chilean content creator Sofikimmy is building a growing following for her League of Legends streams and blazing a trail for Latina gamers everywhere.
bio: From a young age, Sofia 'SofiKimmy' Aravena knew video games would play an important role in her life. The Chilean gamer was introduced to video games by her brother, sharing the classics of the PlayStation 1 and the Nintendo 64. At six years old, she started playing Ragnarok Online and was instantly hooked. At 12, SofiKimmy found her next great game love, League of Legends.

In 2017, at the age of 15, she had the energy and drive to earn herself a following as a new streamer, especially in the world of LoL, a game that stood out for her from a very young age, but various technical matters weren't working in her favour. Two years later, the pieces finally fit. She improved her computer skills, got a good connection and turned on her first stream.
While League of Legends has been a constant favourite, the games that really excite her are The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.
Sofikimmy wants to keep doing what makes her happy. She doesn't dream of unimaginable wealth or global fame, but of continuing to grow, improving as a streamer, as a person and as a content creator.

athletes.name: Sorato Anraku
athletes.standfirst: Japan's Sorato Anraku is an Olympic silver medallist and Boulder world champion who has won four consecutive overall Boulder titles and an overall Lead title.
athletes.discipline: Climbing Boulder / Climbing Lead / Climbing Combined
bio: Sorato Anraku first tried sport climbing as a second-grade elementary school student in his hometown of Yachiyo, Japan. Less than a decade later, he was competing at the highest level of the sport, winning the overall Boulder and Lead World Cup titles in his debut senior season before taking Olympic silver at Paris 2024.

At the 2021 Youth World Championships, Anraku announced himself on the international stage by winning gold in Lead and silver in Boulder. He successfully defended his Lead title in 2022 and added a Boulder bronze.

Anraku stepped up to the senior World Cup circuit in 2023 at just 16 and immediately made history. He won three Lead events and one Boulder event, alongside two further podium finishes, to claim the overall titles in both disciplines in his debut season. He became the first climber to win both the men's Boulder and Lead World Cup series titles in the same season.
He also claimed Lead silver at the 2023 World Championships in Bern before adding Boulder & Lead gold at the Asian Games later that year.

In 2024, at just 17, Anraku won Olympic silver in the men's Boulder & Lead event at Paris 2024. Later that year, he secured his second consecutive overall Boulder title and won Boulder gold at the Asian Championships in Tai'an, China.

Anraku continued his rise in 2025, securing a third consecutive overall Boulder title after reaching the podium at all six Boulder World Cup events. He then claimed his first senior world title with Boulder gold at the World Championships in Seoul at the age of 18.

In 2026, he raised the bar again. Anraku won the opening five Boulder events of the World Climbing Series in Keqiao, Bern, Madrid, Prague and Innsbruck. The streak set a new men's record for consecutive Boulder victories and secured him a fourth straight overall Boulder title with an event still remaining.

After graduating from Yachiyo High School in spring 2025, Anraku chose to turn professional and focus fully on climbing. With an Olympic medal, a world title and four consecutive overall Boulder crowns already secured before turning 20, his career is still only beginning.

athletes.name: Terry Adams
athletes.standfirst: Competing in demos and contests around the world, American rider Terry Adams continues to pioneer the sport of flatland BMX.
bio: Terry Adams could rest on the countless contest wins he's earned around the world, but he chooses instead to take every opportunity to promote the sport he is so passionate about. "Flatland is my heart and soul," he says. "I will do everything I can to help it grow."

Growing up in Hammond, Louisiana, a small town about an hour outside of New Orleans, Terry discovered BMX Flatland when he was 12. Severe asthma and dyslexia made homeschooling a necessity, but that didn't affect his riding aspirations. "I wouldn't say that those things were obstacles," he says. "If you want something bad enough, you can do whatever you want in this world. You just need to believe."
Terry began competing in flatland contests at 16, and since then has amassed an impressive number of awards and accolades, including an X Games gold medal and two NORA Cup wins.

These days, in between competing and continuing to pioneer his discipline, Terry is now widely regarded as the ambassador for flatland, taking part in demos across the world and remaining a world-class Athlete in competitions.

athletes.name: Tomoki Nojiri
athletes.standfirst: The Japanese SUPER GT racer is a also a two-time Super Formula champion.
bio: Tomoki Nojiri attended a racing kart school from an early age and began competing in the All Japan Karting Championship in 2003. He won the championship in 2006, and the following year, he travelled to Europe to compete in the European Championship, Italian Masters and World Cup KF1.

In 2008, he graduated from SFS-F (Suzuka Circuit Racing School Formula) at the top of his class, and in 2009, he began participating in the Formula Challenge Japan. Nojiri steadily gained points through races, and after finishing two seasons at the top of the rankings, he stepped up to All Japan F3 (currently Super Formula Lites).

In 2013, Nojiri finished the F3 season in fourth place in the rankings, surpassing his team-mate, and earned a seat in the following season of SUPER GT and Super Formula. In his debut year in Super Formula, he won the front row twice in qualifying and his first victory in round 6. In SUPER GT, he demonstrated his ability by demonstrating top-class speed and achieving a third place podium finish in the second race.

In 2019, he transferred to Team Mugen and participated in Super Formula. In 2020, he finished the season with good results, recording one win and two pole positions, scoring points in six of the seven races.

In 2021, his first-class abilities, both in terms of skills and experience, bloomed beautifully. He won three times and finished in the top six in Super Formula. He then finished fifth in the sixth race and earned points, clinching his long-awaited title without waiting for the final race. In 2022, Nojiri's momentum continued, finishing in fifth place or higher in all races and winning two of those races, achieving his second consecutive Super Formula victory.
Despite two more overall podium finishes in 2023 and 2024, Nojiri is yet to get his hands on the title again. But he'll keep fighting for that third championship.

athletes.name: Victor Great 'Khalamanja' Ayere
athletes.standfirst: A hugely popular streamer and content creator, Victor Great 'Khalamanja' Ayere is part of a growing wave of professional African gamers.
bio: A pioneering professional gamer and popular content creator from Nigeria, Victor Great 'Khalamanja' Ayere has amassed a huge following across Africa and is widely recognised as one of the continent’s most popular gaming personalities.

Achieving this success has not come without challenges. When Khalamanja first started gaming, the esports industry in Africa was in its infancy and a career in gaming seemed more like a dream than a reality.

Khalamanja’s family were also sceptical, especially his mother, who was keen for him to pursue a more traditional career. However, once he started creating gaming content and began to earn money, they saw his dedication and drive to succeed in the gaming industry and gave him their full support.

Through his streams and social media content, Khalamanja quickly amassed a huge following and is now widely recognised as Africa’s biggest gaming content creator. He has also emerged as a champion for the entire gaming industry in Africa, promoting it as a viable career path and highlighting it as a safe space for young people across the continent.

athletes.name: Wael Arakji
athletes.standfirst: Wael Arakji is a Lebanese basketball player who plays shooting guard for Beirut Club in his domestic league and for the Lebanon national team internationally.
bio: Wael Arakji is one of the stars of pro basketball in Lebanon. He's known for his ability for doing what it takes to win matches – if his team needs to defend, you’ll find him defending like a lion in the defence, and prepare yourself to witness something legendary when he attacks.
Arakji has played in many leagues around the world during his career, turning out for teams in Kuwait, Lebanon, China, the USA, Qatar and Tunisia.

He has a huge list of accolades to his name that includes winning the Tunisian Basketball League and Tunisia Basketball Cup with US Monastir, the Qatar Basketball League with Al-Shamal and five Lebanese league titles with Beirut Club and Al Riyadi Beirut.
The shooting guard wants to be remembered as one of the best players in his position in the Middle East and North Africa region – and it seems he's well on his way to achieving that aim.

athletes.name: Yahya Al Ghassani
athletes.standfirst: A star in Emirati football, Yahya Al Ghassani is recognised as one of the brightest talents in the UAE, set to star for club and country for many years to come.
bio: Yahya Al Ghassani is a professional footballer from Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, who currently plays as a winger for UAE Pro League club, Shabab Al Ahli in Dubai.
He rose through the youth ranks at Dubai’s Al Ahli before signing his first professional contract with Abu Dhabi’s Al Wahda in 2018 to participate in the UAE Pro League.

After a series of promising displays, in 2021 Yahya transferred to Dubai club Shabab Ahli, where he continued to shine, culminating in a standout performance in the 2023 UAE Super Cup match that saw him score two goals as his team romped to a 6-2 victory over Sharjah.

Yahya was soon rewarded with a place in the UAE squad for the 2023-24 AFC Asian Cup. He scored in the UAE's opening match of the tournament, a 3–1 win over Hong Kong. The 2024-25 season saw him playing in the AFC Champions League Two, and scoring two goals in the 26th Arabian Gulf Cup that same season.

In 2025-26, Yahya played in the AFC Champions League Elite, and featured prominently for the UAE in the 2026 FIFA World Cup Asian qualifiers. He continues to be a staple on the left wing, known for his speed and agility, contributing both domestically in the UAE Pro League and internationally.

athletes.name: Yndiara Asp
athletes.standfirst: Brazilian skateboarder Yndiara Asp developed her skills in the bowls of Florianópolis and is a rising star on the skate park scene.
bio: Yndiara Asp was born in Florianópolis and spent her adolescence honing her skateboarding skills in the Brazilian city’s Hi Adventure bowl.
"Growing up in Florianópolis is what made me choose this lifestyle I have today.

“In Florianópolis, especially in the Rio Tavares neighborhood, we live a lifestyle connected to Californian skateboarding,” Asp says. “[It’s all about] pools and skateboarding tracks at home. We have the Hi Adventure, one of the main skateboarding hubs in Florianópolis, which is a meeting point for all the different generations.”

There was always a strong influence towards playing sport in her family. Her father, a keen surfer, made sure Yndiara and her brother were given every opportunity to go out and enjoy themselves whether it be out surfing, playing football or riding bikes.

At the age of seven, her father bought her a skateboard as a Christmas gift. "This was when skateboarding came into my life, the first seed that was planted." But it was only when she was 15 that skateboarding that she began to take things a lot more seriously in terms of her ability.
All that hard work has paid off and today she's a prodigious talent with some impressive early achievements in her skate career.

Yndiara’s first big results came on home soil, with two second-place finishes at Vans Park Series and Oi STU events in São Paulo, before she made her big breakthrough with an attention-grabbing win at Red Bull Bowl Rippers in Marseille, France. She also represented her country in Tokyo at the Games in 2021.

She believes being a good professional skateboarder isn't just about skating well and taking part in competitions. “It’s about being your best version in all parts of your life. As a skateboarder in the park, as a person on a daily basis. It’s being able to communicate, telling your story.”
Right now Yndiara is competing at many Skate Total Urbe (STU) events in Brazil and her long-term goal is to represent her country at the world stage in 2024.

athletes.name: Zoe Backstedt
athletes.standfirst: A junior world champion in road and a two-time cyclocross U23 champ, British rider Zoe Bäckstedt is earmarked as a star of the future.
bio: Growing up in a small village just outside of Cardiff in Wales, Zoe Bäckstedt was quickly introduced to the world of cycling by her parents. Her father Magnus won the famed Paris-Roubaix race and her mother, Megan Hughes, was also a professional cyclist.

Despite growing up in a cycling-centric family – her sister, Elynor, is also a professional cyclist – Zoe initially enjoyed playing netball and tennis, and it was only at the age of 10 that she decided to solely concentrate on pursuing a career on two wheels.

The decision certainly proved to be the correct one as Zoe quickly began to impress in the junior ranks. She racked up numerous national titles before making her mark on the world scene in 2020 when she won a Junior UCI World Cup race, having turned 16 just two months previously.

2021 then proved to be a breakout year for the young rider as she impressed across numerous disciplines. At the UCI Road World Championships, she claimed gold in the junior women’s road race and silver in the junior time trial. She also set a new junior individual pursuit world record and was part of a team pursuit world record riding squad.

Her remarkable rise continued in 2022 when Zoe defended her road race title and upgraded her junior time trial silver to gold at the World Championships. She then won a second world junior title, this time in the cyclocross discipline, before making it a hat-trick of world titles in different disciplines by winning the madison at the UCI Junior Track Cycling World Championships.

Having stepped up to the Under-23 category in 2023, Zoe made the big decision to relocate to Belgium. The move quickly paid dividends as she secured two silver medals at the Cyclocross World Championships.
Zoe claimed gold in the 2024 UCI Cyclocross World Championships under-23 women’s race, backing it up in 2025 with her second successive U23 title.

Proving why she's a threat across multiple disciplines, Zoe won the U23 individual time trial at the 2025 UCI Road World Championships before claiming her first professional general classification title at the Baloise Ladies Tour, becoming the youngest winner in the race’s history.

The following year, Zoe claimed her first UCI Women’s WorldTour stage win at the Tour de Suisse. She also won the British elite road race and time trial national titles, becoming just the third rider to win the race in conesutive years.

Zoe made her Tour de France Femmes debut with Canyon//SRAM in 2026, completing the nine-stage race from Lausanne to Nice. Her standout performance came in the stage four individual time trial, as she missed out on a podium place by just two seconds.

The British rider carried her strong form through to the UCI Road World Championships in Montréal as she powered through the technical 39.2-kilometre course to claim a silver medal behind Marlen Reusser of Switzerland in the elite time trial.

"In the first half, when I heard the first time check, I was thinking, 'OK, maybe it's possible [I can win]'. But I also knew that Marlen was super strong and that she has a very big engine," Zoe said after the race. "So I knew that it was possible that she would bring a lot of time back on me and she did, so massive respect to her."
Still at the very start of her career, it seems only a matter of time before the Welsh rider is chasing world titles at senior level, whether that’s on the track, the road or cyclocross.
